items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: I worked with one of those guys, you know, by the name of Albert Livrat [?]. We played beguines

ctx.x: See, they like the other music, they like their music. The Guadeloupe have their own thing, one of them, one of the music, one of the types of music that the Guadaloupians and the Martinique folks - they had a beguine, they call it, I think. A form of, I used to play it, I worked with one of those guys, you know, by the name of Albert Livrat [?]. We played beguines, it's a kind of a - well, I don't know, got a drum beat, it's somethin' like a bossa nova, you know. More, more than a bossa nova, more rhythm, you…

Well, back to the Philadelphia area in 1918. You sem to be saying something a little bit different than you were saying on Friday - Friday the 4th, this is Sunday the 6th. You gave a stronger and more positive reaction to Lonnie Polk. First of all, he spelled his name P-O-L-
